page.layout: One column of running text, full width. Page number top left, running head top centre. Catchword at the lower left, faint.

main_text.p: Apogæum ejus tempore Ptolomæi erat in ii.[?] gradu virgi-nis, nuncin 6. libræ: Perigæum in 6. arietis, unde cum per primos arietis gradus incedit, Soli oppositus, fulgentissimus appa-ret, ut quandoq; etiam umbram spargat, quoniam tunc epicy-clus in ima eccentrici parte versatur.

Terminus & punctum maximæ latitudinis septentriona-lis est 27. gradus libræ, meridionalis 27. gr. arietis: maxima vero elongatio seu latitudo Jovis in epicyclo, & quidem apogæo & parte septetrionali est unius gr. 6. min. in perigæo 2. gr. & 5. min. Meridionali vero & apogæo unius gr. 4. min. In perigæo 2. grad. 8. min.
Arcus visionis est 10. grad. Stationes ejus fiunt in trigono, hoc est, distantia à Sole 120. grad. Sexannis cum dimidio fere septentriones versus deviat, quinq; cum semisse versus meridiē.

Mars Planeta in ordine tertius, coloris semper rutilantis, naturæ calidæ & siccæ vehementer. Zodiacum interdum egre-ditur, & quidem cum est in opposito augis, sed tamen raro, ut anno 1529. quo per dies 40. fere in mense Julio habuit latitudi-nem 7. graduū. Ex membris habet, fel, venas & renes: ex morbis tertianas, & calidiores omnes, vulnera item faciei: ab Astrologis dicitur infortuna minor. Ex lapidibus habet Jaspidem & Hæmatitem. Ex metallis ferrum: ex plantis calidas & siccas immoderatè, saporisq; fellei & acris. Ex climatibus, tertium, Septen-trionem, Gothiam, Longobardiam, Ferrariam. Motus ejus pe-riodicus est 2. annorum, & 67. dierum: motus diurnus 27. mi-nut. Zodiacum percurrit motu proprio biennio fere. Apo-gæum ejus tempore Ptolomæi erat in 25. grad. Cancri, hodie in 27. Leonis. Maxima latitudo septentrionalis Martis est in 27. Leonis, meridionalis in 27. Aquarii. Extrema latitudo epicycli in septentrione & apogæo est unius gr. 6. min. in perigæo 2. gr. 5. min. In meridie vero & apogæo, 0. gr. 2. min. In perigæo 7. gr. 30. min.

page.notes: Lines 1 and 2 of the first paragraph: "ii." before "gradu" is a faint roman numeral and may be read as "n." in print; marked [?]. "nuncin" is printed as one word. The catchword "Apo-" at the lower left is faint and marked as doubtful. Page is otherwise clear; the running head is set in spaced capitals (DISCVRSVS) and is given here as printed in small capitals. The "&" and "Hæmatitem" ligatures are transcribed as they appear.
